conflicts.point: Whether physical compute tracking (such as 10^26 FLOP thresholds) provides a viable regulatory anchor or merely institutes an anti-competitive licensing cartel.

positions.stance: Argues that tracking massive compute clusters is a necessary and verifiable safety perimeter to prevent uncontained dual-use diffusion.
Argues that compute thresholds serve primarily to erect regulatory moats that protect incumbent cloud monopolies and burden independent developers.

conflicts.point: Whether open-source distribution of model weights acts as a primary vector for defensive security patching or an unrecoverable risk vector for malicious actor access.

positions.stance: Maintains that permissionless open-source diffusion maximizes societal defense by enabling rapid community auditing and deployment.
Maintains that un-gated dissemination of frontier model weights creates irreversible cyber-physical risks that outweigh decentralized patch benefits.
